name: Lesing-Gelimi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only SIL survey wordlists (MacKenzie/Spencer/Van Cott 2011; Hoopert & Wakefield 1980); sil.org blocked 403; no phonology known

sources.citation: Spencer, Juliann, Sara Van Cott & Bonnie MacKenzie. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Amio-Gelimi Language Area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-017. Dallas: SIL International. 101 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Appendix A 'Characteristics of the language' (pp. 37-39) gives only tables of observed consonant and vowel phones, possessive suffixes and word-order examples; no word on stress, accent or syllable structure; the App. C.1 wordlists carry no stress marks (0 occurrences of the IPA stress mark or accented vowels in the whole text layer).

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives listing for [let] (Internet Archive copy 2015-09-17 of sil.org/resources/search/language/let).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists exactly two SIL holdings for the language: the 2013 survey report and Hoopert & Wakefield 1980; no phonology, grammar or dictionary exists in SIL's archive.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-146: Lesing-Gelimi -> Amio-Gelimi (submitted by Sara Van Cott, SIL-PNG).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; establishes the naming: Amio + Kaskas villages = Amio dialect, Atui + Poronga = Gelimi dialect; 'lesing' means 'language' in the Amio dialect.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. xiii+487 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Treats 'Atui (Lesing)' only in comparative tables and cognate sets (pp. 161-163, 167, 183-184; informants p. 398: John Aiom of Amio, Fabian Vilang of Atui). No statement about stress for Atui/Lesing; the book's only stress remarks concern Ali/Schouten languages (Verner-type lenition).
Glottolog lists no descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference at all, only Ross 1988 pp. 160-173 for subclassification and the SIL survey wordlists; Wikipedia has no phonology section.

sources.citation: PARADISEC audio item for Lesing-Gelimi [let] (1 OLAC record with audio, 2021 dump; probably Malcolm Ross's 1980s Atui/Amio wordlist recordings).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Primary audio from which stress placement could be observed instrumentally if no written statement exists; catalog blocked (not reachable by automated download) by automated download.
